title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the Longue Marche cycle (1981). On the preceding pages Grothendieck has defined 'L-groups' (groupes à lacets: a group with distinguished conjugacy classes of 'loops' or inertia generators, modelled on the fundamental groups of punctured surfaces or 2-orbifolds). He has also defined 'LT-groups', which are extensions of a Teichmüller-type group T by an L-group pi, and has just observed that the GT-hat group, as an extension of Teichmüller groups by pi, appears as an LT-group.

Section 2 ('profinite case') says the profinite version of these notions is essentially evident. In the profinite setting the LT-structure is expressed through germs of exterior homomorphisms (8) K_i^g : T -> pi. He then announces 'the most important example for us'.

The example: let k be a field (the restriction 'algebraically closed of characteristic 0' is crossed out). Let M be an algebraic 'multiplicité' over k, meaning in modern terms a Deligne-Mumford stack (orbifold), assumed to be:
- 0-connected,
- of finite type over k,
- geometrically [connected],
- smooth of relative dimension 1.
So M is an orbifold curve, possibly with generic stabilizer.

He states as something one 'should be able to prove': M can be presented as M = (U,G), where U is a smooth quasi-projective curve over k and G is a finite group acting on U. (U,G) means the small ringed topos of G-equivariant étale sheaves on U, i.e. the quotient stack [U/G].

The next page gives the purpose. He wants a finite étale (Galois) cover of M that is a scheme. He then forms the exact sequence 1 -> pi_1(U) -> pi_1(M) -> G -> 1, transports the L-structure of the surface group pi_1(U) to pi_1(M), and so obtains profinite L-groups from orbifold curves. These are the building blocks for the profinite Teichmüller tower and GT-hat.
errors: The global-quotient claim is false in the generality stated. M is allowed to be proper. Over C, the 'bad' 2-orbifolds (the teardrop P^1(n), and the spindle P^1(m,n) with m != n) are smooth proper DM curves with no finite étale cover by a scheme. Their orbifold fundamental group is trivial or finite cyclic and does not kill the stabilizers. Hence they are not of the form [U/G] with U a scheme and G finite. The correct statement (Behrend-Noohi, 'Uniformization of Deligne-Mumford curves', 2006; classically Bundgaard-Nielsen-Fox over C) requires excluding these bad cases, or stabilizer-order conditions.

Grothendieck himself flags the existence of a scheme as a finite étale cover as only conjectural ('Plus intriguant, il doit être vrai...', next page). On this page 'on doit pouvoir prouver' is likewise a conjecture, not a proof.

Possible gap: over non-closed k, or with non-trivial generic stabilizer, banded gerbes over curves need extra care. Whether every such gerbe is a [U/G] with G finite is not addressed. This is minor relative to the bad-orbifold issue.

ideas.what: Profinite version of groups with loops (L-groups) and of LT-groups, expressed via germs of exterior homomorphisms T -> pi
ideas.modern_name: profinite 'groupes à lacets' / profinite surface groups with inertia data and outer actions of Teichmüller groups (Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Longue Marche); developed by Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps and others
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, now edited); Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in outline

ideas.what: Description of a 1-dimensional smooth DM stack ('multiplicité') as the topos of G-equivariant étale sheaves on a smooth quasi-projective curve U
ideas.modern_name: orbifold curve as global quotient stack [U/G]; uniformization of DM curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fox / Bundgaard-Nielsen (topological case); Behrend-Noohi 2006 (algebraic DM curves); Kresch-Vistoli 2004 (finite flat covers and quotient presentations)
ideas.where_published: Multiplicités modulaires are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific statement may appear in the Longue Marche

ideas.what: Using the exact sequence 1 -> pi_1(U) -> pi_1(M) -> G -> 1 to transport an L-structure to the orbifold fundamental group (next page)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of an orbifold curve as a profinite Fuchsian-type group with inertia classes

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates around 1981 a uniformization conjecture for algebraic orbifold curves: every such curve is [U/G] and admits a finite étale cover by a scheme. This anticipates Behrend-Noohi's 2006 work, but omits the bad-orbifold exceptions. It is a historical precedent rather than a new result.
missed.quote: On doit pouvoir prouver alors que M peut se décrire par une courbe alg. lisse et quasi-projective U sur k, un groupe fini G qui opère sur U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only. The correct theorem is now known, and the statement as written is false for teardrop and spindle orbifolds.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a setup page. It extends L-groups to the profinite case and conjectures that orbifold curves are global quotients. That conjecture is now a known theorem, with exceptions Grothendieck did not note. It is historically interesting as an early formulation, but nothing here is absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: 'qui soit {+de t.f. sur k,+} [-lisse-] géométriquement' is likely meant as 'géométriquement 0-connexe' (or similar) followed by 'et lisse de dimension relative 1'. The word read as 'dimension' appears to be 'dim. relative'.
The inserted '{+pi+}' above 'L-groupe' is plausibly an insertion making it 'L-groupe pi'.
In the margin by (9), '(petit)' is attached to 'Topos annelé'.
